question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{4} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{4} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
